items.title: Jon Hendricks — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I was very relieved when I talked with Duke. We went up to his suite in the Fairmont one night, just Judith and me. Duke talked to us all night long.

ctx.x: I was too shy. That’s like asking Duke Ellington, can I sing with his band? I was terrified. I’m a very shy person. I really still am very shy. It took me three years to say hello to Ella Fitzgerald. She kept saying, “It’s about time. I was wondering when you . . . .” I’m always very shy about things like that.
I would never have known that. Your music is tremendously outgoing.

items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: He and Duke Ellington had that same thing

ctx.x: Yeah. They didn’t know what to do with that.
Yeah. Because they hadn’t heard that. But that’s the essence of American popular music is the, as Duke says, “it don’t mean a thing if it ain’t got that swing.”
Did you have a musical family?

items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I was surprised when he told me that all he wanted to have was an orchestra that would approach Fletcher Henderson’s.

ctx.x: I don’t want to do that. I’m very aware that if it hadn’t been for these people I may never have done what I did.
Well even Ellington had his influences, and that kind of pulled a lot of things together to make his sound.
I was surprised when he told me that all he wanted to have was an orchestra that would approach Fletcher Henderson’s. I said whoa.
